Tutorial: Ask a side question with /btw, fork it, and switch back with the arrow keys

/btw lets you ask a question about the current session without adding it to the conversation history. If the answer needs real tool access (reading a file, running a command), press f in the answer overlay to spin the question into a forked subagent that inherits the whole conversation. The fork runs in a panel below your prompt while you keep working in the main session, and ↑/↓ moves the panel's selection between the main session's row and the fork's row.

Can each hackathon team share one API key through Claude Enterprise connectors, and how does ChatGPT secrets management differ?

Short answer: Neither product has a general secrets vault that a team member can add a key to. Claude's closest feature is a custom connector with a stored request header, which an Owner sets up once for the organization, so team members never handle the key. ChatGPT's closest features are GPT Action API-key auth and Codex cloud environment secrets.

Codex cloud secrets. Answer/Official from OpenAI: Cloud environments. Secrets are an environment-level setting with an extra layer of encryption, decrypted only when a task runs. They are available to setup scripts only and are removed before the agent phase, so the agent itself cannot read them. The page does not say who can edit secrets or whether workspace members share them. For Codex work, this is the nearest thing to a managed secret in ChatGPT, but it exists for running a repository, not for giving chat or a GPT a key.

What can do that Claude/Code can't do, and vice versa?

Short answer: Cowork and Code run the same underlying Claude agent and sub-agent task-decomposition approach, but wrap it in opposite operating surfaces — Cowork is a GUI tab in Claude Desktop built for knowledge work on documents and data inside explicitly granted folders; Code is a terminal/IDE agent built for codebases with full filesystem access, code execution, and git. Each has capabilities the other structurally lacks.

Code: runs in a terminal or inside an IDE (VS Code, JetBrains); operates with the user's full filesystem authority, no folder-mounting step required.

How can I make sure a Claude/Routine in Claude/Desktop/Code has all the permissions it needs to run, since there's no obvious way to set automatic permission mo

Short answer: It depends which of the two things Desktop's Routines page created. A Cloud routine has no permission-mode picker at all — that's by design, not a gap: cloud routines always run autonomously with no approval prompts, and their reach is bounded by repositories, the cloud environment, and connectors instead. A Local scheduled task does have a permission-mode picker and a per-task "always allow" approval list — if that's the control that seems to be missing, it's likely because Cloud was picked instead of Local when the routine was created.

Answer/Official from Automate work with routines and Schedule recurring tasks in Claude Code Desktop:
How can I make sure a Claude/Routine in Claude/Desktop/Code has all the permissions it needs to run, since there's no obvious way to set automatic permission mo

Cloud routines (Desktop → Routines → New routine → Cloud): "Routines run autonomously as full Claude Code cloud sessions: there is no permission-mode picker and no approval prompts during a run." What a cloud routine can reach is scoped by the repositories selected (and their branch-push rule), the environment's network access and variables, and the connectors included — not by a permission mode.
How can I make sure a Claude/Routine in Claude/Desktop/Code has all the permissions it needs to run, since there's no obvious way to set automatic permission mo

Local scheduled tasks (Desktop → Routines → New routine → Local): these do have a permission mode. The instructions form "includes pickers for the permission mode and model," set per task at creation or edit time; allow rules from ~/.claude/settings.json also apply to scheduled-task sessions.
How can I make sure a Claude/Routine in Claude/Desktop/Code has all the permissions it needs to run, since there's no obvious way to set automatic permission mo

Getting a Local task to run with full automatic permission: if a task runs in Ask mode and hits a tool it isn't allowed to use, the run stalls in the sidebar until approved. To avoid that: click Run now right after creating the task, watch for permission prompts, and choose "always allow" for each one — future scheduled runs then auto-approve those same tools without prompting. Saved approvals can be reviewed or revoked later from the task's "Always allowed" panel on its detail page.

One caveat: MCP tools an organization set to ask, or any tool marked requiresUserInteraction, always prompt and never offer an always-allow option — a task calling one of those stalls on every run regardless of permission mode.

Bottom line: not finding a way to set automatic permission is expected for a Cloud routine — there's nothing to configure, since it's already unattended. For a Local scheduled task, the setting exists; the durable "no more prompts" state comes from one manual Run now with "always allow" clicks, not from a single toggle.

Short answer: There's no built-in "merge" or "promote" button — a side chat is intentionally one-way (it can read the main thread, but nothing inside it writes back). If you want to keep something it produced, copy the relevant text yourself and paste it into the main session's prompt box, then close the side chat.

Why there's no automatic merge: The official docs describe the feature as explicitly not adding anything back to the main conversation — that's the point of it (avoid steering the main session off course).
How do I add content from a Claude/Desktop/Code side chat back into the main session?

Requests for a real merge-back exist but aren't shipped: Issue #10370 — "Chat Branching: Spawn side-chain conversations with selective merging back to main" proposed /merge-to-main / /merge "<summary>" commands for exactly this workflow. It gathered supportive comments through early 2026 but was auto-closed for inactivity without being implemented, so manual copy-paste remains the only path today.

Practical workaround: Select and copy the useful part of the side chat's response, paste it into the main thread as your own message (optionally with a short "from the side chat:" framing), then close the side chat.
